CookingGraph.description: The internal DAG of a recipe: what the LLM extracts, what the scheduler consumes.

cuisine.description: Cuisine, when the source states or implies one.

servings.description: Servings the quantities are stated for.

stages.description: Ordered stages; every node's `stage` must appear here.

stated_total_min.description: Total time the original recipe claimed. Sanity-checks extraction (§5.8).

CookingPlan.description: The scheduled, renderable output the user sees.

critical_path.description: Node ids on the longest path.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph this plan was computed from.

saved_min.description: serial_min - total_min. The number the product is arguing for.

scheduled.description: Every node, placed on the timeline.

serial_min.description: Sum of all typical durations, done one at a time.

warnings.description: Safety-check findings (§4.5). "degraded" means extraction fell back.

windows.description: Wait windows derived from the timeline.

Ingredient.description:
One ingredient line from the source recipe.

A `prep_note` is a hint that a prep node exists: "2 onions, finely chopped"
implies a `chop_onion` node even when no written step mentions chopping.

group.description: Ingredient grouping, e.g. "For the masala" / "For garnish".

optional.description: Optional ingredients are exempt from the consumption invariant (§5.5).

prep_note.description: Preparation stated on the ingredient line, e.g. "finely chopped".

qty.description: Quantity, or null when the recipe gives none.

Node.description:
One unit of work in the cooking graph.

`kind` and `attention` are separate on purpose. `attention` decides whether the
node occupies the cook and therefore whether it creates a wait window; `kind`
decides how it renders. Scheduler code must branch on `attention` only.

attention.description: Whether the cook is occupied. `unattended` and `periodic` create windows.

consumes.description: Ingredient ids and/or component ids this node uses up.

depends_on.description: Node ids that must COMPLETE before this node may start.

doneness_cue.description: Sensory finish signal, e.g. "onions light golden, oil separating".

duration_max.description: Pessimistic duration; window-safety checks use this.

duration_typical.description: Duration the plan displays and schedules on.

instruction.description: Full sentence(s) shown in step mode.

interruptible.description: Whether the cook can drop this mid-way and return. Gates `periodic` windows.

kind.description: Render classification. Not used by the scheduler.

label.description: UI heading, four words or fewer.

max_lead_min.description: Freshness ceiling: minutes this may finish before its consumer starts (§4.5).

produces.description: Component id this node yields, e.g. "comp_base".

stage.description: Id of the stage this node belongs to; must exist in `stages`.

station.description: The resource this node contends for.

tip.description: Optional aside shown in step mode.

RecipeListResponse.description: Every recipe the API can currently serve.

RecipePlanResponse.description:
Everything the Plan view needs, in one round trip.

The graph rides along because the plan is node *ids* and timings — the labels,
instructions and ingredients the renderer draws all live on the graph. Shipping both
keeps the frontend a pure renderer: it joins by id, and computes nothing.

stages.description: Per-stage rollups, in `graph.stages` order. See schedule/rollup.py.

RecipeSummary.description: One row in the recipe list.

id.description: Slug used in the plan URL.

servings.description: Servings the quantities are stated for.

ScheduledNode.description: One node placed on the timeline.

end_min.description: Minutes from the start of cooking.

node_id.description: Id of the node in the source graph.

occupies_cook.description: Whether the cook is busy for this interval. Follows `Node.attention`.

rank_in_window.description: Order within the window. 0 is the task the UI promotes as "start with this".

start_min.description: Minutes from the start of cooking.

window_id.description: Set when this ran inside another node's wait window.

value.description: The URL, the image reference, or the pasted text itself.

Stage.description:
A named group of nodes: Prep, Cook Base, Add Veggies, Finish.

Stages are user-facing and ordered; the Plan view groups by them.

color_key.description: Key into the stage palette in docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md.

StageSpan.description:
A stage's footprint on the scheduled timeline.

Deliberately NOT part of `CookingPlan`: it is a view over a finished plan, computed
by `abc_cook.schedule.rollup`, and adding it to the plan would rewrite all five
golden fixtures for a rendering convenience.

It exists because the Plan view shows a per-stage minute count, and the frontend is
forbidden from deriving one (CLAUDE.md). Stages interleave — in Kadai Paneer `prep`
spans 0-19 while `cook_base` spans 3-22 — so a stage is a span, not a block.

elapsed_min.description: Wall-clock span of the stage. Overlaps other stages' spans.

end_min.description: Latest end among this stage's nodes.

inline_work_min.description: `work_min - windowed_work_min`. What the stage's own card still shows.

node_ids.description: This stage's nodes, in scheduled order.

stage_id.description: Id of the stage in the source graph.

start_min.description: Earliest start among this stage's nodes.

windowed_work_min.description: Of `work_min`, the minutes absorbed into another stage's wait window.

work_min.description: Sum of `duration_typical` over the stage's nodes.

WaitWindow.description:
An unattended interval the scheduler filled with prep work.

User-facing as "while this cooks". Capacity is deliberately below the host node's
duration — see §4.3 for the multipliers and why they exist.

assigned.description: Node ids, in the order the cook should do them.

capacity_min.description: Usable minutes, after the safety multiplier.

host_node_id.description: The unattended or periodic node whose duration creates it.
